page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top centre with page number at top left. Main text in one column of italic type with ">>" quotation marks at the line starts. Two marginal notes in the left margin beside the fourth and fifth lines of the text block ("4.Eiusdē." and "3. Eiusdē."). Catchword and signature absent.

main_text.p: ratione morbi, vt cū dixit, Mulsam aut vinū, vtrū magis auxiliaturū putaueris. Secundo, causa imbecillitatis virtutis, vt cū dixit, His ita habētibus si venter liquidus fuerit corpus absumens &c. Tertio, ratione consuetudinis. Hoc est quod Galenus oīauo de methodo dixit: Constat aut et Hippocrate nō in diarijs modo febribus, verū etiā in acutis, ex ijs quæ de acutarū victu prodit, vinū dare &c. Ostensum igitur est, quod cum consuetudo morbi multum vrgentis indicationi dissentit, cum esse exhibendum potum, in quo minimum sit consueti, multum verò curātis: Hunc dicimus aquosum consuetum, vt vinum aquosum ijs qui vino sunt assueti. Quòd si Anglo cernisiæ potui assueto acuta febris accidat, modicum cernisiæ ei assuetæ multa aqua hordei miscebimus, & ei ministrabimus.
Sed vt reliqua quisq; in promptu habeat, tabellam secundam apponemus, à qua facilè horum singula haberi possunt. Sed illud scire oportet, quod quæ de consuetudine loquentes hucusq;

page.notes: The page is a sixteenth or seventeenth century Latin medical text. Marginal notes "4.Eiusdē." and "3. Eiusdē." are in the left margin. The opening line shows the printed quotation marks as ">>" marks. Several words in the scan are faint or show-through from the reverse, notably near the lower left, and were not transcribed. Some italic words such as "Anglo" and "cernisiæ" are read as printed and may be uncertain [?].
